# TickPulse (WoW Forever)

![TickPulse logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Shambels/tickpulse/main/media/TickPulse-logo-400.png)

TickPulse shows a rotating overlay on your periodic aura icons that resets on every tick:

- DoTs: the swipe goes from one damage tick to the next.
- HoTs: the swipe goes from one heal tick to the next.

This branch targets the **WoW Forever** client (`## Interface: 16001`). The original TBC Anniversary build is in git history before `0.2.0`.

## Install

1. Create a folder named `TickPulse` in your WoW Forever addons directory.
2. Copy `TickPulse.toc`, every `.lua` file and the `media` folder into that folder (or link the repository folder, see below).
3. Launch or reload the game (`/reload`).

Typical path:

`World of Warcraft/_forever_/Interface/AddOns/TickPulse/`

## Quick update script (Windows)

Run this from the repository root in PowerShell:

`./deploy-addon.ps1`

By default it copies repository files (excluding `.git` and the script itself) to:

`C:\Program Files (x86)\World of Warcraft\_forever_\Interface\AddOns\TickPulse`

Optional custom destination:

`./deploy-addon.ps1 -Destination "D:\Games\WoW\_forever_\Interface\AddOns\TickPulse"`

## Commands

- `/tpulse show`
- `/tpulse hide`
- `/tpulse scan`
- `/tpulse options`
- `/tpulse debug`
- `/tpulse debug player|target|focus`

- `/tpulse test` / `/tpulse test off`
- `/tpulse frames`
- `/tpulse spells`, `spell`, `interval`, `add`, `remove` (see "Per-spell settings")

`/tpulse debug` also prints the client interface version and whether aura data is currently readable or secret.

## Test mode

Addons cannot put real auras on you, so `/tpulse test` (run out of combat) fakes them:

- A small draggable "TickPulse test" frame shows a fake DoT icon (3s ticks, 15s duration) and a fake HoT icon (2s ticks, 10s duration). Both restart when they run out, so you can also watch the ticks-left count and the clip warning. Use it to check the swipe, the numbers, opacity and the Settings toggles.
- If you have any buff (food, a class self-buff), a fake 3s tick schedule is attached to its icon on the real buff frame. This tests matching against Blizzard's buff buttons. It follows the "Show ticker on player auras" toggle.

`/tpulse debug test` lists the test trackers and which button each one is bound to (`(missing)` means the real buff icon could not be matched). `/tpulse test off` removes everything.

## Ticks left and clip warning

- **Ticks left** (off by default): a small number in the icon's top-right corner shows how many ticks the aura still has. It needs a known duration, so it's missing for auras whose duration TickPulse hasn't seen yet.
- **Clip warning** (on by default): recasting a Classic-era DoT or HoT restarts its tick timer, which throws away the progress toward the next tick. In the last two ticks of your own aura, the swipe turns red during the second half of each tick. Recast while it isn't red.

## Cast bar tick marks

While you channel a spell, TickPulse draws a mark on your cast bar for each tick. Marks for ticks that already happened are dimmed, so you can stop the channel right after a tick instead of wasting part of one. Your own cast info stays readable in combat, so this works fully on Forever.

It covers the aura-tracked channels (Mind Flay, Drain Life, Drain Soul, Drain Mana, Evocation, Tranquility, First Aid bandages) plus Arcane Missiles, Blizzard, Rain of Fire, Hellfire, Health Funnel, Hurricane and Volley. Pushback moves the end of the channel and the marks are redrawn to match.

## Options

- Open with `/tickpulse options` (or `/tpulse options`), or go to Options -> AddOns -> TickPulse.
- Settings are saved per account in `TickPulseDB`.
- Toggles:
   - Show ticker on player auras
   - Show ticker on target frame
   - Show ticker on focus frame
   - Track other players' HoTs/DoTs on you
   - Show rotating ticker
   - Show numeric values on ticker
   - Show ticks left
   - Warn before clipping a tick
   - Flash the icon on each tick
   - Play a sound on each tick (your own auras only, throttled)
   - Show tick marks on the cast bar
   - Overlay opacity slider (0% to 100%)
   - Colours: DoT swipe colour (gold), HoT swipe colour (green), and an optional last-tick colour (orange, off by default), each with a colour picker. The clip warning's red takes priority over the last-tick colour.
   - Reset visual defaults (numeric off, rotating on, opacity 65%, default colours)

## How it works on WoW Forever

WoW Forever runs on the modern client and applies the same addon restrictions as Midnight:

- Addons cannot register the combat log (`COMBAT_LOG_EVENT_UNFILTERED`), so TickPulse can no longer see ticks happen.
- While restrictions are active (combat, encounters, PvP), aura data is *secret*: addons can pass it to the UI but cannot read or compare it.

Classic-era DoTs and HoTs tick on a fixed schedule from the moment they are applied, so TickPulse predicts the ticks:

1. **Aura data readable** (usually out of combat): the tick schedule is anchored at `expirationTime - duration` from `C_UnitAuras`. This is exact, and covers refreshes and auras cast by other players.
2. **Aura data secret** (usually in combat): your own spellcasts are still readable. When you cast a tracked spell, TickPulse anchors the schedule at the cast time. Durations learned while auras were readable are saved and used to expire trackers.
3. **Never-hidden spells**: the client can mark individual spells as never secret. TickPulse asks `C_Secrets.ShouldSpellAuraBeSecret` for each tracked spell. For the ones that stay readable, it keeps reading your real auras in combat instead of predicting from the cast. `/tpulse debug` lists those spells and marks their trackers "live aura data".
4. When restrictions lift (leaving combat, encounter end), TickPulse rescans and corrects everything from real aura data.

## Known limitations

These come from the client's addon restrictions and need in-game confirmation:

- While auras are secret, matching an overlay to the right Blizzard icon depends on the icon's texture or aura instance ID being readable. If Blizzard hides those too, overlays for spells applied *during* combat may not appear until combat ends. Overlays bound before combat stay attached.
- While auras are secret, TickPulse cannot see auras that other players apply to you, and it cannot tell whether your cast was resisted.
- For projectiles (Fireball, Pyroblast, Serpent Sting, Viper Sting) the aura lands after the cast, so their in-combat schedule is only started from aura data.
- When you switch target or focus, TickPulse parks the old unit's trackers by GUID and restores them when you switch back (kept until they expire, or 2 minutes if the duration is unknown). If the client hides the unit's GUID, the trackers are dropped instead. The new target's own auras still can't be read until restrictions lift.
- Talents or effects that change tick speed are not learned anymore: there is no combat log to learn from. Use `/tpulse interval <spell> <seconds>` if a spell ticks differently.

## Per-spell settings and custom spells

- Options -> AddOns -> TickPulse -> **Spells** shows a table of your class's tracked spells (plus First Aid and your custom spells) with columns for **Name**, **Category** (DoT/HoT), **Timer** (seconds between ticks) and an **Enabled** checkbox. Overridden timers are shown in yellow with a `*`. Hover a row for its spell ID and default timer.
- Commands:
   - `/tpulse spells`: list your class's spells, their tick interval and whether they are on.
   - `/tpulse spell <spellID|name> on|off`: turn a spell on or off.
   - `/tpulse interval <spellID|name> <seconds|reset>`: override a spell's tick interval, for example after a talent changes it.
   - `/tpulse add <spellID> <seconds> [dot|hot] [self]`: track a spell that isn't in the list, such as one of Forever's new abilities. `self` means the aura lands on you even with a target selected.
   - `/tpulse remove <spellID>`: forget a custom spell.
- Settings are stored per spell ID in `TickPulseDB` (`spellOverrides`, `customSpells`), so they apply to every rank of the spell. A newly added custom spell is tracked immediately and the Spells table updates the next time it is opened.

## Unit frame addons

TickPulse draws on Blizzard's buff, target and focus frames by default. It also attaches to these addons automatically a few seconds after login:

- **ElvUI**: player, target and focus unit frame auras, plus the player buff and debuff headers.
- **Shadowed Unit Frames**: player, target and focus unit frames.

`/tpulse frames` re-runs the detection and prints what it found.

Other addons (EllesmereUI, custom frames, WeakAuras-style displays) can register their aura buttons with the public API:

```lua
-- auraType: "HELPFUL" for HoTs, "HARMFUL" for DoTs, or "ALL" (default)
TickPulseAPI.RegisterAuraContainer(myTargetDebuffFrame, "target", "HARMFUL")
TickPulseAPI.UnregisterAuraContainer(myTargetDebuffFrame)
```

The frame can be a container (its descendants are searched) or a single aura button. Buttons need an `Icon` or `icon` texture region. Setting `button.auraInstanceID` lets TickPulse match buttons exactly instead of by icon.

## Tracked spells

`spells.lua` lists the Classic-era 1-60 periodic spells for all nine classes, plus First Aid (every bandage heal aura is named "First Aid"). Matching is by localized spell name, so all ranks are covered. Each entry also has an enUS name fallback in case the client cannot resolve the spell ID. A few later-expansion spells are kept in case Forever's new abilities reuse them; they are ignored when the spell does not exist.

## Development

- Every push and pull request runs [luacheck](https://github.com/lunarmodules/luacheck) through GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/luacheck.yml`), using `.luacheckrc`. It catches syntax errors, typos in globals and unused variables before you load the game.
- To run it locally, install Lua and LuaRocks, then `luarocks install luacheck` and run `luacheck .` in the repository root.
- When you use a new WoW API global, add it to `read_globals` in `.luacheckrc`.

## Releases (CurseForge / Wago / GitHub)

Releases are built by the [BigWigs packager](https://github.com/BigWigsMods/packager) (`.pkgmeta`, `.github/workflows/release.yml`):

1. Commit your changes and push a tag, for example `git tag v0.3.0` then `git push origin v0.3.0`.
2. The workflow replaces `@project-version@` in the TOC with the tag, builds `TickPulse-v0.3.0.zip` without the development files, and attaches it to a GitHub release.
3. To also upload to CurseForge and Wago:
   - Uncomment the `X-Curse-Project-ID` and `X-Wago-ID` lines in `TickPulse.toc` and fill in your project IDs.
   - Add `CF_API_KEY` and `WAGO_API_TOKEN` as repository secrets on GitHub (Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions).

When the addon is loaded straight from the repository (for example through a junction), the in-game version shows as `@project-version@`. That's expected; packaged builds show the tag.

The packager picks the game version from `## Interface: 16001`. If CurseForge or Wago doesn't map that to WoW Forever yet, the upload step may need a game version override; the GitHub release still works.

# TickPulse

## [v0.3.0](https://github.com/Shambels/tickpulse/tree/v0.3.0) (2026-11-08)
[Full Changelog](https://github.com/Shambels/tickpulse/commits/v0.3.0) [Previous Releases](https://github.com/Shambels/tickpulse/releases)

- Set CurseForge project ID for tagged releases  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Add TickPulse logo and addon list icon  
    Move the logo into media/ with a PNG for the README and a TGA used as the  
    addon list icon (## IconTexture). The README shows the logo and the  
    install steps include the media folder; the packager skips the source  
    SVG and the README PNG.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Show the Spells settings page as a table  
    Replace the vertical checkbox list with a canvas page that has Name,  
    Category (DoT/HoT), Timer and Enabled columns, zebra-striped scrolling  
    rows and a tooltip with the spell ID and default timer. Overridden timers  
    are highlighted, and the table rebuilds when opened or when spells change  
    from chat, so custom spells appear without /reload.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Add CurseForge/Wago packaging and tag release workflow  
    Pushing a v* tag runs the BigWigs packager, which fills in  
    @project-version@ in the TOC, builds a zip without development files and  
    attaches it to a GitHub release. CurseForge and Wago uploads turn on once  
    their project IDs are added to the TOC and the API keys are set as  
    repository secrets.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Add unit frame addon support and public aura container API  
    New integrations.lua exposes TickPulseAPI.RegisterAuraContainer and  
    UnregisterAuraContainer so other addons can add their aura buttons to the  
    search, and auto-registers ElvUI and Shadowed Unit Frames aura frames  
    after login. /tpulse frames re-runs the detection and reports it.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Add per-spell settings and custom spells  
    Each tracked spell can be turned off or given a different tick interval,  
    and spells missing from the list can be added by ID. Overrides and custom  
    spells are saved per spell ID in TickPulseDB and applied to running  
    trackers immediately. A new Spells settings page lists the player's class  
    spells with on/off checkboxes; /tpulse spells, spell, interval, add and  
    remove manage them from chat. Seed spells are now tagged with their class.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Add DoT, HoT and last-tick swipe colours  
    DoTs and HoTs now have separate swipe colours (gold and green by default),  
    with an optional last-tick colour. Colours are chosen with the colour  
    picker from the Settings panel, saved in TickPulseDB, and reset with the  
    other visual defaults. The clip warning keeps priority over them.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Add optional tick flash and tick sound  
    When a predicted tick happens on a visible overlay, optionally flash the  
    aura icon and/or play a short click. The sound only plays for your own  
    auras and is throttled so several DoTs ticking together make one click.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Add ticks-left count and clip warning  
    Overlays can show the number of ticks an aura has left, and in the last  
    two ticks of your own DoT/HoT the swipe turns red during the second half  
    of each tick, when recasting would throw away more than half a tick.  
    Test-mode icons now have a looping duration so both can be checked.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Add channel tick marks on the player cast bar  
    New castbar.lua draws a mark on PlayerCastingBarFrame for each tick of a  
    channelled spell and dims marks once their tick has passed, so a channel  
    can be stopped right after a tick. Covers aura-tracked channels plus  
    Arcane Missiles, Blizzard, Rain of Fire, Hellfire, Health Funnel,  
    Hurricane and Volley, redraws on pushback, and has a Settings toggle.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Add luacheck config and GitHub Action  
    Runs luacheck on every push and pull request with a Lua 5.1 standard and  
    an explicit list of the WoW globals the addon reads or writes, so syntax  
    errors and global typos are caught before loading the game.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Remember trackers per target across target swaps  
    When target or focus changes, park the old unit's trackers by GUID and  
    restore them when that unit is selected again, so DoTs applied in combat  
    survive swapping. Parked trackers expire with their aura, or after two  
    minutes when the duration is unknown. Units with hidden GUIDs keep the  
    old behaviour of dropping their trackers.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Read live aura data in combat for never-hidden spells  
    While aura data is secret, ask C\_Secrets.ShouldSpellAuraBeSecret for each  
    tracked spell and look up the ones that stay readable by name, so their  
    trackers use real timing in combat instead of the cast-time prediction.  
    Aura tables whose timing fields are secret no longer wipe a known schedule.  
    /tpulse debug lists the never-hidden spells and marks live trackers.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Add /tpulse test mode for debugging without real auras  
    Shows a draggable frame with fake DoT and HoT icons on fixed tick  
    schedules, and attaches a fake tick schedule to one of the player's real  
    buffs to exercise matching against the Blizzard buff frame.  
    /tpulse debug test reports the bindings; /tpulse test off clears it all.  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Port TickPulse to the WoW Forever client  
    Forever runs on the modern client (Interface 16001) with Midnight's addon  
    restrictions: the combat log can't be registered and aura data is secret  
    during combat. Ticks are now predicted from each aura's application time  
    (aura data when readable, the player's own cast when not) instead of being  
    observed from the combat log.  
    - Use C\_UnitAuras/C\_Spell and guard every aura value against secrets  
    - Match aura buttons on the modern player/target/focus frames  
    - Move options to the Settings panel and persist them in TickPulseDB  
    - Update the spell list for Classic-era 1-60 spells; fix bandage matching  
    - Point the deploy script and README at the \_forever\_ folder  
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>  
- Add chanelled spells  
- Add License  
- Added bandages  
- Add options  
- Update UI  
    Ticks now show on player top-right corner auras  
- Add "update" script for addon deployment  
- Update addon to overlay default spell icon  
    Instead of rendering in a separate frame  
- Initial commit
